claims.text: As-solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn has a fine cellular microstructure.
As-solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn has a high dislocation density.
Nanoscale Mn-rich precipitates are uniformly distributed at cell or grain boundaries in as-solidified FeNiCrMn.
The Mn-rich precipitates are analogous to Mn2O3.
Rapid solidification generates a high density of dislocations in FeNiCrMn.
At low-to-moderate temperatures and strain rates, the nanoscale precipitates hinder dislocation motion through Orowan looping.
Orowan strengthening by the precipitates enhances yield strength.
Orowan strengthening by the precipitates enhances ductility.
At elevated temperature or high strain rate, the precipitates exert Zener drag.
Zener drag retards dynamic recrystallization and recovery in FeNiCrMn.
Retarded recrystallization and recovery preserve dislocation structures and delay mechanical softening.
The transition from Orowan strengthening to Zener-drag-mediated recrystallization delay governs the dynamic behavior of FeNiCrMn.
The proposed precipitate-mediated interplay maintains a favorable strength-ductility balance over a wide range of dynamic loading regimes.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit high yield strength at low-to-intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit high ductility at low-to-intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
Yield strength will generally decrease as test temperature rises.
Dynamic recrystallization will begin later in precipitate-bearing FeNiCrMn than in systems lacking pronounced nanoscale precipitates.
Delayed dynamic recrystallization will produce more gradual mechanical softening.
Classical slip and twinning dominate deformation at room temperature and approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Significant changes in precipitate morphology or volume fraction, or microstructural coarsening during testing, may invalidate the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: A strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1 is called quasi-static in the intervention but is called moderate in the baseline.
